threads.body: [General] `SENTINEL` is also a container command supported across this instrumentation's Rediscala range, but its command classes are named `SenMasters`, `SenSlaves`, `SenGetMasterAddr`, etc., rather than starting with `SENTINEL`. Consequently these requests still emit values such as `SENGETMASTERADDR` instead of stable `db.operation.name=SENTINEL`, retaining the incorrect per-subcommand series this change is intended to remove. Please map Rediscala's `Sen*` command names to `SENTINEL` (a prefix-to-operation mapping can handle the differing names) and cover one of these commands in the tests.

replies.body:
Fixed in 89a3c07. You're right, and the prefix allowlist could not catch these because the class names don't start with `SENTINEL`.

I read the encoded command string out of each class's constant pool to confirm rather than guessing from the name: `SenMasters` holds `SENTINEL MASTERS`, `SenGetMasterAddr` holds `SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name`, `SenSlaves` holds `SENTINEL SLAVES`, `SenResetMaster` holds `SENTINEL RESET`, `SenMasterInfo` holds `SENTINEL master`, and `SenMasterFailover` holds `SENTINEL FAILOVER`. All six now map to `SENTINEL` through an explicit class-name-to-command map that is consulted before the prefix allowlist.

That same map now also covers the other classes whose name is not the command rediscala sends, such as `ZrangeWithscores` to `ZRANGE` and `Renamex` to `RENAMENX`, and there is a separate rule that strips the trailing `$` from no-argument commands, which were reporting `PING$`.

I did not add a Sentinel test. Exercising one needs a running Redis Sentinel rather than the plain Redis container this module starts, which is a lot of test infrastructure for one map entry. The map itself is covered by the new `zrangeWithscores` test, which asserts `ZRANGEWITHSCORES` under old semconv and `ZRANGE` under stable.
